title: Salt and Thorn Anew
premise: Vesper Ashgrove, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent her life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow and the old gods cannot see. When prayers begin to be answered again—first by a dying pilgrim who names her heir to a dead god's covenant—she learns the valley's silence was not sanctuary but a seal her ancestors forged at terrible cost. Carrying the covenant's secret out of the Hollow, Vesper is hunted by the Thorn Court, godlings who feed on answered prayer, while the covenant itself whispers that it can only be renewed through her blood. In the end, Vesper refuses both the war and the throne: she unbinds the covenant entirely, returning divinity to mortals as memory rather than power, and chooses to remain in the valley—not hidden this time, but free.
about_author: Emrys Oyelaran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from mountain communities before turning to fiction. Their work blends folkloric cadence with sharp political imagination, exploring what people inherit and what they owe.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She tends graves and sharpens a sword she swore never to draw, establishing the Hollow's magic-dead quiet and her oath-bound isolation. A stranger collapses at the valley's edge, praying aloud—and something answers. Emotional beat: the unease of a life built on stillness beginning to crack.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Covenant
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The pilgrim, Ilan, dies of wounds no mortal blade made, pressing a bone sigil into her hand and naming her 'heir of the Ashgrove line.' The sigil burns with a voice that knows her grandmother's name. Emotional beat: grief entangled with dread as inheritance arrives unwanted.

chapters.title: What the Elders Buried
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She confronts Maren, the valley's eldest, who admits the Hollow was sealed deliberately: the founders traded their gods' voices for peace after a catastrophic war. Maren begs her to bury the sigil. Emotional beat: betrayal—the sanctuary she trusted was a prison built on a lie.

chapters.title: The First Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Tomas, a young shepherd boy's POV. His desperate prayer for his sick sister is answered by something vast and warm, and the whole valley feels the tremor of returning magic leaking through the failing seal. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into communal fear.

chapters.title: Thornlight on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Watching the ridge at night, she sees figures walking where nothing should live: emissaries of the Thorn Court, drawn by the leak in the seal. They leave a message carved in living bramble: return what you carry. Emotional beat: the hunter's chill of being seen at last.

chapters.title: Oath and Iron
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Forced to defend Tomas's family from a thorn-creature, she draws her sword and speaks the first words of power in a generation—the swordspeech answering without her consent. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration fused; the oath is waking whether she wills it or not.

chapters.title: Leaving the Hollow
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. With the seal failing and the Court closing in, she leaves the valley carrying the sigil, accompanied reluctantly by Tomas, whose sister now bears a faint divine mark. Emotional beat: sorrowful resolve—exile chosen so others may keep their peace.

chapters.title: The Road Remembers
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Outside the valley, the world is saturated with half-waking shrines and frightened villages. He watches Vesper struggle with a world that worships fearfully. Emotional beat: awe tempered by homesickness; the ordinary world is stranger than stories said.

chapters.title: The Godling's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A minor godling named Serevain offers protection from the Thorn Court in exchange for a taste of the covenant's power. Vesper refuses, but the encounter reveals the Court wants not the sigil—it wants her, the last vessel capable of renewing a god. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being a prize rather than a person.

chapters.title: Ashgrove Histories
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In a ruined monastery library, she reads her family's true history: the Ashgroves were not protectors but jailers, bound to a god they executed to end the war—and the covenant can resurrect it through an heir's willing death. Emotional beat: horror at discovering her lineage's founding sin.

chapters.title: Marked
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The Thorn Court captures them briefly; Tomas bargains with his sister's mark to buy escape, learning the Court plans to use Vesper's blood to crown a new war-god and rule through answered prayer. Emotional beat: guilt and growing loyalty—he owes her more than he can repay.

chapters.title: The Whispering Blade
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The covenant begins speaking through her sword at night, offering visions of the old war and promising peace if she surrenders herself. She starts to doubt whether refusing is wisdom or cowardice. Emotional beat: seduction of martyrdom; power whispering in the language of duty.

chapters.title: City of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the capital, they find dozens of fledgling godlings squabbling over worshipers, corrupt and petty—power's corruption made visible. Vesper witnesses a miracle bought with a child's memory. Emotional beat: revulsion sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: An Old Soldier's Debt
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She seeks Brey, her grandmother's former comrade, now a drunk innkeeper, who confesses the Ashgrove women were meant to die at thirty to keep the seal fed—and her grandmother fled the duty, dooming the valley's silence to fail. Emotional beat: rage and pity braided together; her whole life reframed.

chapters.title: The Court's Invitation
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The Thorn Queen offers Vesper a place at her side: become a goddess, spare her friends, reshape the world kindly. Vesper nearly accepts—until she sees the Queen's courtiers, hollow-eyed and memory-stripped. Emotional beat: temptation at its most reasonable and therefore most dangerous.

chapters.title: What Tomas Prayed For
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. His sister's mark grows; the Court comes for her as a secondary vessel. Tomas prays again—deliberately this time—and the answer costs him his happiest memory. Emotional beat: sacrifice revealing what power truly charges.

chapters.title: Breaking the Oath
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Understanding that the covenant feeds on oaths, Vesper formally breaks her ancestral vow before witnesses, weakening the god's hold—but freeing the seal fully, letting all the old powers flood back into the world. Emotional beat: liberation shadowed by catastrophe unleashed.

chapters.title: The War That Wakes
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Across the land, old grievances ignite as gods choose champions; armies muster under resurgent banners. Veper realizes breaking the oath started the very war she feared. Emotional beat: despair at unintended consequence; the weight of choice.

chapters.title: The Throne of Brambles
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She walks into the Thorn Court's heart to face the Queen, offering herself—not to be crowned, but to be heard. She demands the covenant be unbound, its god left dead, its power returned as memory. Emotional beat: courage stripped of glory; negotiation as battlefield.

chapters.title: Salt and Thorn
chapters.summary: Climax. Vesper's POV. The Queen refuses; battle erupts between Vesper's swordspeech, Tomas's marked defiance, and the Court's host. Vesper drives the sigil into the covenant's heartstone, shattering divinity itself into countless mortal memories. Emotional beat: ferocious, costly triumph—power dissolved rather than seized.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Miracles
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The world reels: no more answered prayers, but everyone carries a fragment of the divine as memory and dream. Some grieve the loss; many feel lighter. Tomas recovers one lost memory—a gift from the shattered covenant. Emotional beat: bittersweet mourning turning toward hope.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She returns to the Hollow, which opens its borders freely for the first time in generations. She plants thorn roses on her grandmother's grave, takes students who wish to learn the swordspeech as craft, not power, and stays—not hidden, but home. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; inheritance transformed into choice.
